description.narrative: (Somalia): ..Bar Ama Baro (BAB, "Teach or Learn" in Somali), will increase access to quality education for out-of-school children and youth between ages 9-17 in 17 districts spanning Mogadishu, South West State, Hirshabelle, and Jubaland. In partnership with the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS), BAB will increase student enrollment; school safety, literacy, numeracy; and socio-emotional skills acquisition. The program will also support greater government capacity to regulate accelerated basic education. With FY 2022 funds, BAB will revise and distribute learning materials developed for overage learners to complement the government's formal curriculum. Furthermore, USAID will assist the government and the private sector to develop accelerated basic education (ABE) programming and policies on teacher qualifications, instructional time, and academic standards. This latter effort will lead to accreditation of ABE and certification of students so that they may transition into formal schools at the right level. BAB will also foster positive gender norms and reduce educational barriers for girls and boys. In addition, community efforts to support education - from advocacy, mobilization and protection of vulnerable students - will help build resilience to withstand Al-Shabaab's ideological attacks and coercive recruitment techniques. At the same time, BAB is pivoting programming to respond to Somalia's ongoing drought, the country's worst in over 70 years. Specifically, BAB will focus on enabling students to continue to learn during the crisis and will target an additional cohort of learners displaced by the drought. This program complements the planned New Somalia Education Support and Adolescent Girls Education programs (co-funded with the UK)...... ... ........ ..
